canonical_sources.title: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm

pedagogy.problem_statement: In a distributed network where servers can crash and messages can be delayed or lost, how do multiple independent nodes agree on a single, shared, sequential history of state?
pedagogy.core_thesis: Raft achieves consensus by decomposing the problem into leader election and log replication: a single leader elected by a majority quorum broadcasts append-only log entries to followers.
pedagogy.mental_model: A parliamentary committee where members elect a temporary chairperson; no policy can be enacted into law unless a strict majority of members sign the exact same ledger entry.
pedagogy.key_takeaway: Consensus requires a stable leader and majority log commitment across terms.
verified_claims: At most one leader can be elected in any given term (Election Safety).
A leader never overwrites or truncates its own log entries; it only appends.
An entry is committed once replicated across a majority quorum of nodes.
If a server applies an entry at a given index, no other server will ever apply a different entry for that index.
anti_patterns: Do not imply all nodes must agree simultaneously; a majority quorum (N/2 + 1) is sufficient.
Do not show followers accepting writes directly from clients; all mutations must route through the leader.
Do not confuse consensus with simple gossip protocols; log ordering is strictly linear and verified.

entities.name: Server Node Cluster
entities.role: Distributed nodes maintaining identical replicated state machines

entities.name: Current Term Counter
entities.role: Logical clock dividing time into discrete election terms

entities.name: Majority Quorum Bound
entities.role: Minimum votes required to elect a leader or commit an entry

entities.name: Append-Only Log Entry
entities.role: State mutation carrying term, index, and state machine command

equations.spoken_form: Votes received must be greater than or equal to floor of N divided by two, plus one
Election timeout sampled uniformly between one hundred fifty and three hundred milliseconds

algorithmic_steps.state_effect: A follower's heartbeat timer elapses, transitioning to Candidate in a new term
Candidate gathers majority votes and transitions to Leader
Leader transmits log entry to followers via heartbeat waves
Majority acknowledgement commits the entry into local state machines

visual_metaphors.motion_pattern: Radial pentagonal cluster layout with state ring status
Node transitions from blue follower to glowing amber leader with crown badge
Concentric ripple rings expanding outward from leader to all followers
Log slots turn from uncommitted amber to committed emerald green

scene_blueprint.title: The Consensus Problem
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Establish the distributed challenge: independent nodes must agree on an ordered log despite network delays and crashes.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: 5-node pentagon cluster materializes; question badge appears over desynchronized nodes.

scene_blueprint.title: Leader Election
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Demonstrate leader election: a timeout triggers a candidate, requesting votes until a majority quorum is reached.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Node S1 timeout fires; vote request beams travel to peers; 3 of 5 vote yes; S1 crowns as Leader.

scene_blueprint.title: Log Replication
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Show log replication: the leader receives client writes, broadcasts AppendEntries heartbeats, and followers replicate.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Client write arrives at leader; heartbeat waves broadcast entries; follower logs illuminate in parallel.

scene_blueprint.title: Quorum Commitment
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Explain consensus commitment: once written to a majority quorum, the entry is committed permanently and applied.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Majority acknowledgement count hits 3/5; log slots turn solid emerald green; cluster reaches consensus.
